name: Tanzanite-Desolation
description: Tanzanite-Desolation is a tidally locked ice world whose sunward hemisphere displays a haunting blue-violet coloration caused by mineral inclusions in the surface ice, the precise trichroic shift that gives tanzanite its character. The frozen landscape glows in shades of sapphire and lavender under the perpetual gaze of its star, while the dark side plunges into temperatures that freeze atmosphere itself. Crystal caverns riddle the transition zone between light and dark, their formations grown over millions of years of slow sublimation.

The twilight band where the two hemispheres meet is the only region where surface conditions are survivable, and even there the cold is punishing. The crystal caverns ring with faint harmonic tones caused by thermal expansion and contraction, creating an eerie natural music that echoes through kilometers of ice. The violet light on the sunward side has a quality of intensity that makes colors appear more vivid than they should, as though the ice amplifies rather than filters the spectrum.

Ruins were discovered in the largest crystal cavern, structures of unfamiliar alloy half-enclosed by ice growth that dates their exposure at over ten thousand years. The builders are unknown, and the ruins' purpose is unclear, though the structures are oriented toward the subterranean ocean below. Microbial life thrives in that ocean, metabolizing exotic matter traces in a biochemistry that has no terrestrial analog.

Tanzanite-Desolation's exotic matter deposits and platinum veins make it commercially valuable, but the ruins have triggered heritage protection protocols that freeze all extraction claims. The connection between the ruins and the subsurface ocean suggests the ancient builders knew something about this world that modern science has yet to discover. The crystal caverns continue to sing their cold, clear notes, indifferent to the jurisdictional disputes playing out above.
